name: Emails That Get Replies
lede: You know what you want to say — now say it clearly, politely, and once. These are the phrases that make a request easy to answer, so you stop rewriting the same email five times.
outcome: Clear, polite, and confident — the email you send once, and the reply you actually get.
outcomes: Open with the ask so the reader knows what you need before the second line.
Sound polite without padding every sentence, and firm without sounding cold.
Follow up once or twice in a way that moves things forward, not nagging.

aside.title: Written for the email you keep drafting.
aside.body: Short, natural lines for asking, chasing, and closing a thread — without reading it over ten times.

words.definition: Sending a second message about something you asked about before.
words.example: I’m following up on my email from last Tuesday.

words.definition: At a time that is suitable for you.
words.example: Please review the draft at your convenience this week.

words.definition: In a way that matches what has just been said.
words.example: The budget changed, so please update the plan accordingly.

words.definition: Referring back to something agreed in an earlier talk.
words.example: Per our conversation, I’ve attached the revised quote.

words.definition: A gentle way to ask for an update without pressure.
words.example: Just checking in to see if you saw my note.

words.definition: To copy someone into an email so they can see it.
words.example: Please cc me on the reply to the client.

words.definition: To send a hidden copy of an email to someone.
words.example: I’ll bcc my manager so she has the context.

words.definition: To answer everyone who was copied on the original email.
words.example: Please don’t reply all — just send it to me.

words.definition: To send an email you received on to someone else.
words.example: I’ll forward the client’s email to the design team.

words.definition: A file that is sent together with an email.
words.example: The attachment is too large to send by email.

words.definition: A chain of emails on the same topic.
words.example: Scroll down the thread to see my earlier reply.

words.definition: The short title at the top of an email.
words.example: Put the project name in the subject line.

words.definition: A situation where something is arranged only a little before it happens.
words.example: Sorry for the short notice, but the meeting moved to noon.

words.definition: A quick warning or early information about something.
words.example: Thanks for the heads-up about the deadline change.

words.definition: To make something clearer by explaining it in more detail.
words.example: Could you clarify the deadline for the second draft?

words.definition: To say officially that something is true or will happen.
words.example: Please confirm the new meeting time by Thursday.

words.definition: A polite ask for something you need from someone.
words.example: I’ve sent a request for the updated figures.

words.definition: To be grateful for something someone has done.
words.example: I really appreciate you turning this around so quickly.

words.definition: A quick answer that comes without much delay.
words.example: Thank you for your prompt reply to my question.

words.definition: Used to say there is no need to hurry.
words.example: No rush, but could you send it by Friday?

words.definition: The actions that need to happen after this point.
words.example: I’ve listed the next steps at the bottom.

words.definition: To feel pleased about something that will happen soon.
words.example: I look forward to hearing your thoughts on Monday.

words.definition: To contact someone, usually to ask or offer something.
words.example: I’m reaching out about the invoice from March.

words.definition: Before something happens, rather than at the time.
words.example: Please send the slides in advance of the meeting.

words.definition: To give someone regular updates as things develop.
words.example: I’ll keep you posted once the client replies.

words.definition: To reply to someone after checking or thinking.
words.example: I’ll get back to you by end of day.

words.definition: To say sorry for a mistake or a delay.
words.example: I apologise for the delay in sending the file.

words.definition: Short and clear, with no unnecessary words added.
words.example: Keep the email concise so people actually read it.
